audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for love as surpassing way, gifts without love, love's qualities, partial knowledge, faith/hope/love.

verses.restored: If I speak in the tongues of humans and of messengers, but do not have love, I have become sounding bronze or clanging cymbal.

familiar.text: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

modern.text: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.

original.text: Ἐὰν ταῖς γλώσσαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαλῶ καὶ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, γέγονα χαλκὸς ἠχῶν ἢ κύμβαλον ἀλαλάζον.

verses.restored: And if I have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all trust so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.

familiar.text: And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing.

modern.text: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἐὰν⸃ ἔχω προφητείαν καὶ εἰδῶ τὰ μυστήρια πάντα καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γνῶσιν, ⸄καὶ ἐὰν⸅ ἔχω πᾶσαν τὴν πίστιν ὥστε ὄρη ⸀μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι.

verses.restored: And if I distribute all my possessions, and if I hand over my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.

familiar.text: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.

modern.text: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἐὰν⸃ ψωμίσω πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντά μου, ⸄καὶ ἐὰν⸅ παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου, ἵνα ⸀καυθήσομαι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐδὲν ὠφελοῦμαι.

verses.restored: Love is patient; love shows kindness; love does not envy; love does not boast; it is not puffed up.

familiar.text: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,

modern.text: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

original.text: Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ, χρηστεύεται ἡ ἀγάπη, οὐ ζηλοῖ ⸂ἡ ἀγάπη⸃, οὐ περπερεύεται, οὐ φυσιοῦται,

verses.restored: It does not act disgracefully, does not seek its own, is not provoked, does not calculate the harmful.

familiar.text: Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;

modern.text: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.

original.text: οὐκ ἀσχημονεῖ, οὐ ζητεῖ τὰ ἑαυτῆς, οὐ παροξύνεται, οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν,

verses.restored: It does not rejoice over injustice, but rejoices together with the truth.

familiar.text: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;

modern.text: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.

original.text: οὐ χαίρει ἐπὶ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ, συγχαίρει δὲ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·

verses.restored: It bears all things, trusts all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

familiar.text: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

modern.text: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

original.text: πάντα στέγει, πάντα πιστεύει, πάντα ἐλπίζει, πάντα ὑπομένει.

verses.restored: Love never falls. But prophecies will be made inactive; tongues will cease; knowledge will be made inactive.

familiar.text: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.

modern.text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.

original.text: Ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε ⸀πίπτει. εἴτε δὲ προφητεῖαι, καταργηθήσονται· εἴτε γλῶσσαι, παύσονται· εἴτε γνῶσις, καταργηθήσεται.

verses.restored: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

familiar.text: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

modern.text: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,

original.text: ἐκ μέρους ⸀γὰρ γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν·

verses.restored: But when the complete comes, the partial will be made inactive.

familiar.text: But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away.

modern.text: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.

original.text: ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον, ⸀τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται.

verses.restored: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, thought as a child, calculated as a child; when I became a man, I made inactive the things of the child.

familiar.text: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

modern.text: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.

original.text: ὅτε ἤμην νήπιος, ⸂ἐλάλουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐφρόνουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐλογιζόμην ὡς νήπιος⸃· ⸀ὅτε γέγονα ἀνήρ, κατήργηκα τὰ τοῦ νηπίου.

verses.restored: For now we see through a mirror, in enigma, but then face to face; now I know in part, but then I will know fully, just as I also was fully known.

familiar.text: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.

modern.text: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.

original.text: βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι διʼ ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι, τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον· ἄρτι γινώσκω ἐκ μέρους, τότε δὲ ἐπιγνώσομαι καθὼς καὶ ἐπεγνώσθην.

verses.restored: But now remain trust, hope, love, these three; and the greatest of these is love.

familiar.text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

modern.text: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.

original.text: νυνὶ δὲ μένει πίστις, ἐλπίς, ἀγάπη· τὰ τρία ταῦτα, μείζων δὲ τούτων ἡ ἀγάπη.

translation_notes: Agape is the governing center for all gifts, knowledge, sacrifice, and discipline in 1 Corinthians.
Love is not sentimental softness; it is the durable communal reality without which spiritual power becomes noise.
